setter.name: Derek
setter.evidence: Rep: 'Already got some information from Derek.' Prospect: 'the little link that I got initially... did you get that link from Derek?' 'Yeah, I think so.'

prospect.name: Kathie
prospect.family_status: Has a 30-year-old daughter and a 9-year-old granddaughter; caring for an 86-year-old mother with dementia
prospect.training_background: Trained 2x/week 30 min with a personal trainer in Fairbanks plus elliptical; describes that period as the best shape of her life. Ex-military. Home gym with elliptical, squat bench, pull-up station and three kettlebells (one 30 lb, two 10 lb). Currently inactive, ~6,000 steps/day.
prospect.medical: Postmenopausal, on bioidentical hormones (previously waking at 3 a.m., now sleeping through). Foot/heel surgery in December 2025 repairing three ankle tendons after ~2 years of a misdiagnosed foot problem; ~3 months non-weight-bearing and sedentary; states she is 'finally recovered'. Reports residual balance deficit in the right foot, left hip stiffness, self-reported loss of muscle mass and bone density. Dairy allergy.

signals: Explicitly wants to return to a former self: 'when I was doing personal training, I was in really good shape and I was weighing about 155. So that's my goal.'
Lost ground to a hard season — heel surgery plus menopause: 'since my surgery, I've definitely noticed a decrease in muscle mass and bone density.'
Carries regret about the lost time and the misdiagnosis; frames now as the first moment she is physically able to commit.

goals.text: Get back to around 155 lb from a current 200 lb
Rebuild muscle mass lost to menopause and post-surgical inactivity, and turn the metabolic advantage back on
Regain flexibility, especially the left hip and glutes, and re-address balance in the operated right foot
Maintain bone density through resistance training
Get energy levels back up through the day
Be physically capable at retirement in ~5 years — move to Hawaii and farm/grow vanilla
Keep up with a 9-year-old granddaughter, garden and maintain a large yard
Avoid ending up as limited as her 86-year-old mother with dementia
Short, efficient home workouts that fit around a 3-hour daily commute

pains.text: Post-menopausal muscle loss and insulin resistance — 'once I hit menopause, I hit the wall and the things that used to work for me are not working for me anymore'
Three months of post-surgical inactivity after heel/ankle tendon reconstruction, with measurable loss of muscle and bone density
Left hip stiffness and atrophied glutes; residual balance deficit in the operated foot
Very stressful job — 'the most stressful job I've ever had' — leaving no capacity to force herself to exercise after work
Roughly 3 hours of daily commuting on top of a 7-3:30 workday
Cannot self-start or stay consistent without someone looking over her shoulder
Desk-bound role after previously being in the field
Burned by a previous ~$3,000 fitness app that was fully automated and prescribed unscaled workouts she could not perform
Not confident her kettlebell form is correct and worried about hurting herself
Sleep was badly disrupted before starting bioidentical hormones

objections.rep_response: Reframed as $1,000 a month, did not isolate, did not build a financial picture, later said 'if it comes down to money, of course, then we can find a solution there' without structuring anything

objections.raw_quote: Okay, well, let me think about it overnight and I'll let you know.
objections.rep_response: Asked what the thinking came down to, surfaced the price and the prior bad experience, then agreed she should watch more videos and booked a 30-minute follow-up rather than pressing for a decision

objections.raw_quote: the little link that I got initially, it said it was like $119 a month or something.
objections.rep_response: Explained the $119/mo link is the community product with standard programs and no one-to-one time, and said he would not recommend it for her

objections.raw_quote: I have actually done some of these app things before, and I was really disappointed because basically it was just on autopilot... I think it was around $3,000 or something like that... and then I didn't have any benefit whatsoever.
objections.rep_response: Sympathised ('this sort of makes my blood boil'), asserted Trevor works one-to-one and is not a robot, offered to send a written list of deliverables

objections.raw_quote: does he really have a lot of experience dealing with older women and women in general, you know, and so from a training perspective.
objections.rep_response: Conceded openly that roughly 95% of the coach's clients are men and his experience with women is 'a little bit less', then pivoted to his injury-rehab track record

objections.raw_quote: it's hard to imagine that a person like that would understand where you're coming from when you're, you're older, you're still out of exercise
objections.rep_response: Told the coach's origin story — stiff, injured, not fit, built up over years — and said many clients start injured

evidence: Prospect: 'Okay, well, let me think about it overnight and I'll let you know.'
A 30-minute follow-up call was booked and the calendar invite confirmed live: 'Yeah, 8pm to 9pm is what it's got, yep.'
No payment taken, no payment link mentioned, no verbal agreement to proceed.
Counter-evidence toward a future close: 'I do think it's a valuable investment in myself' and she has followed the brand for a year.
Counter-evidence against: two unresolved trust concerns (burned by a prior $3,000 app; coach's limited experience with older women).
outcome.next_step: 30-minute follow-up call booked for the next day (8 p.m. Bulgaria time); rep to send a written list of programme deliverables; prospect to watch the remaining videos.

notable.note: Prospect had a major foot/ankle tendon reconstruction in December and a residual balance deficit in that foot, and is being moved toward loaded kettlebell training with no question asked about surgical clearance. Separately the rep openly disclosed that ~95% of the coach's clients are men and that his experience with women is less — honest, but it left a live objection unresolved and is a repeatable positioning problem for a female prospect. A $119/month community tier surfaced from the setter's link and had to be untangled from the $6,000 offer.

quality.notes: Frequent inversions. Whole rep turns are attributed to 'Kathie' and vice versa — e.g. at 00:01:37 the prospect's disclosure of her own foot surgery is labelled as the rep, and at 00:02:29 the prospect's statement of her three goals is labelled as the rep. Roles were resolved from content throughout.
